papers.title: Ergothioneine Mediated Neuroprotective Effects in the Nervous System.
papers.abstract: Ergothioneine (EGT), a micromolecular derivative of histidine containing sulfur, is found in various organisms, including humans. It demonstrates antioxidant properties, reduces inflammation, and potentially possesses antiaging effects for neurodegenerative conditions, positioning EGT as a potential candidate for health enhancement and healthy aging. EGT appears to offer strong protective properties at the cellular level and shows decreased concentration levels in blood plasma in different neurological conditions such as cognitive impairment, Parkinson's disease, macular degeneration, and other neurodegenerative diseases. Further, emerging evidence from both preclinical and currently limited clinical studies indicates EGT's therapeutic potential for neurological disorders. For instance, EGT treatment slowed the progression of age-related hearing loss and alleviated the cisplatin-induced hearing loss in mouse models, especially in male mice. Similarly, EGT intervention in older adults (aged 60 years or older) has shown some effectiveness in improving cognitive ability, memory, and sleep quality. In this review, we present a thorough examination of its function in neuroprotection, particularly within the nervous system and explore its potential intracellular targeting pathways and their underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: An all-in-one analytical platform for rapid determination of toxic dyes in complex water by SERS and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable determination of toxic dyes in complex aqueous environments remains challenging because matrix interference and complicated sample pretreatment often compromise analytical accuracy and practical applicability. Therefore, an integrated filtration-adsorption-SERS sensing platform coupled with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) modeling was fabricated for rapid and quantitative detection of malachite green (MG) and methylene blue (MB) in complex water samples. Polypropylene filter cloth (PPFC) served as a porous fibrous support for sample filtration, while Ag nanoparticles (Ag NPs) were uniformly immobilized on the fiber surfaces via a seed-mediated in situ growth strategy to provide SERS-active sites. Activated carbon was incorporated into the PPFC/Ag filter configuration to provide adsorption of the target dyes during sample treatment. The resulting configuration integrates filtration, adsorption, and SERS detection within a common analytical workflow, while 1D-CNN modeling was employed for quantitative analysis of the acquired SERS spectra. Benefiting from the integrated filtration-adsorption configuration and porous fibrous architecture, the platform exhibited high signal uniformity and favorable analytical performance, with detection limits of 10-9 M for both MG and MB. Adsorption kinetic analysis demonstrated that dye removal followed the pseudo-second-order model, with equilibrium removal efficiencies of 99.7% for MB and 98.6% for MG. To improve quantitative reliability in complex matrices, a 1D-CNN model was employed for SERS spectral analysis, yielding high accuracy with R2 values of 0.992 and 0.982 for MB and MG, respectively, with low prediction errors. Furthermore, spiked Moyan Lake water samples showed recoveries of 98.14% and 96.37% for MB and MG, respectively, with RSD values of 4.53% and 4.91%, demonstrating satisfactory accuracy and precision in a real water matrix. By integrating these complementary functions within the same filtration configuration, the proposed platform establishes a continuous analytical workflow from sample filtration and adsorption to SERS detection and quantitative analysis. This integrated design simplifies the conventional multi-step procedure and provides a sensitive, reliable, and practical approach for rapid monitoring of trace organic dyes in complex water matrices.

papers.title: Validation of an open-source hardware for cardio-physiological studies in fish: A statistical equivalence study with a widely used research-grade electrophysiological recording system.
papers.abstract: Monitoring heart rate (fH) accurately is fundamental for fish eco-physiological studies. However, these measurements rely heavily on expensive experimental tools. Here, we aimed to validate BITalino, an inexpensive, open-hardware biosignal acquisition system for measuring fH that could help to democratize research in fish physiology. BITalino is a modular electrophysiological system with a dedicated electrocardiogram (ECG) module that records ECG signals through electrodes connected to the module via lead wires and attached directly to the subject. We compared BITalino with a widely used research-grade physiological recording system (BIOPAC) by measuring fH in fish using both devices simultaneously. Heart-rate measurements did not differ significantly between devices, and there was no significant Device×Time interaction, indicating that both systems tracked temporal variation similarly. The intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) showed that 85.9% of the variance was due to biological differences between fish, with less than 5% from device-related variance. These results confirm that BITalino can be effectively used for fH monitoring in fish physiology studies. Beyond its low cost, its portability, modular design, open-hardware architecture and compatibility with third-party analysis software make it easily adaptable for different experimental applications, and may facilitate its use in resource-limited research settings.

papers.title: What Is the Association Between Psychosocial Risk Factors and Pain and Function Outcomes in People With Rotator Cuff Disorders? A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe the association between psychosocial factors and pain and function/disability in people with rotator cuff (RC) disorders. DESIGN: Etiology systematic review. LITERATURE SEARCH: Systematic searches were conducted in CINAHL, EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Scopus databases from inception to November 2025. The PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines were followed. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: Studies were eligible if they included adults with RC disorders and examined associations between psychosocial factors and pain and/or functional outcomes. DATA SYNTHESIS: Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool. Due to study heterogeneity, results were presented descriptively. RESULTS: Thirty-eight observational studies (n = 4845; 2024 males, 2170 females, 651 sex not reported) were included. Over 70% of studies were of medium-high methodological quality. Pain catastrophizing (r = -0.50 to 0.62, β = -0.54 to 0.50) and sleep (r = -0.59 to 0.54, β = -0.41) had moderate-to-strong associations with functional outcomes. Fear-avoidance had weak-to-strong associations with function (r = -0.61 to 0.24, β = -0.59 to -0.27, odds ratio [OR] = 1.39). Moderate evidence supported associations between fear-avoidance, sleep disturbance, pain catastrophizing, and functional outcomes. Poorer mental health had a moderate-to-strong association with pain severity (r = -0.52 to -0.48) and impaired function (r = -0.61 to 0.75); the strength of evidence was limited. Weak-to-strong associations with limited strength of evidence were observed between remaining psychosocial factors and pain. CONCLUSION: Pain catastrophizing and sleep disturbance demonstrated moderate-to-strong associations with functional impairment in people with RC disorders. Fear-avoidance beliefs had heterogenous associations with function. Poor emotional health was associated with greater pain severity and functional impairment. JOSPT Open 2026;4(4):420-441. Epub 19 June 2026. doi:10.2519/josptopen.2026.0194.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine Inhibition of GABA Neurons in the Ventral Tegmental Area Attenuates the Depth of Sedation in Mice.
papers.abstract: Dexmedetomidine is a sedative anesthetic with a unique ability to produce an arousable state of sedation. However, the neural mechanisms underlying this arousable sedation remain incompletely understood. Previous studies have implicated dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) in mediating this effect, but the upstream neural circuit mechanisms remain unclear. Furthermore, although VTA GABAergic neurons exert robust inhibitory effects on dopaminergic neurons, their specific role in dexmedetomidine-induced arousable sedation remains unclear. Vgat-Cre transgenic mice were used to investigate the role of VTA GABAergic neurons in dexmedetomidine-induced arousable sedation. Electroencephalography (EEG), fiber photometry, calcium imaging, GABA neurotransmitter sensing, chemogenetic manipulation, and immunohistochemistry were used to assess neuronal activity, GABAergic signaling, and behavioral responses to dexmedetomidine. Fiber photometry using the calcium indicator GCaMP6m revealed that dexmedetomidine inhibited VTA GABAergic neurons. Fiber photometry with the GABA neurotransmitter sensor iGABASnFR demonstrated that dexmedetomidine increased GABAergic input to VTA GABAergic neurons. Chemogenetic manipulation combined with EEG demonstrated that activating VTA GABAergic neurons deepened dexmedetomidine-induced sedation, whereas inhibiting these neurons attenuated sedation. These findings suggest that dexmedetomidine increases GABAergic input to VTA GABAergic neurons and suppresses their activity, potentially contributing to its arousable sedative effects. Further studies are needed to establish the causal role of this neural circuit mechanism.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Measuring solute clearance across brain states: methods and the sleep-brain-drain debate.
papers.abstract: The glymphatic hypothesis posits that cerebrospinal fluid and interstitial fluid bulk-flow clears brain waste, with increased waste transport during sleep. Recent studies reporting the opposite have generated substantial controversy. Three issues underlie the controversy surrounding this hypothesis and are the subject of this reviewMethods:We critically reviewed these three issues. First, we identified heterogeneity in the methods used to quantify brain "clearance" and evaluated their validity, recalculating rate constants from published data where these were not originally reported. Second, we examined uncertainty regarding the physical forces driving fluid and solute movement, and how assumptions about advection influence model specification. Third, we critiqued the dichotomization of brain state into "sleep" and "wakefulness". Clearance rates reported by competing groups fall within a similar range, yet the conclusions drawn about the influence of sleep are diametrically opposed. No gold-standard approach exists either for measuring clearance or for defining and inducing brain states. These conflicting results cannot be adjudicated: the debate persists not because the rates differ but because no shared standard exists to determine whether the opposing state-associations are real. Methodological standardization is a precondition for a reproducible account of how brain solute clearance is regulated.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Persistent Venous Narrowing of Downstream Parenchymal Microvessels and Pial Veins in the Male Mouse Cortex.
papers.abstract: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH), a hallmark of sleep apnea, can lead to cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, though its precise impact on cerebral microcirculation remains unclear. This study investigated the longitudinal effects of 2-week chronic IH (8% O2, 6.5-min cycle for 6 hours/day) on brain microcirculation in the male mouse cortex. We observed a significant reduction in the diameters of pial veins (from 55 to 46 μm) and parenchymal venules (from 9.9 to 8.2 μm) after chronic IH relative to pre-IH conditions, while upstream arteries (47 to 44 μm) and arterioles (12.4 to 12.0 μm) were unaffected. This selective reduction in downstream venule diameter led to a significant increase in arterio-venous transit time, indicating reduced cerebral blood perfusion. Furthermore, neurovascular coupling (NVC) responses showed a substantial decrease, pointing to impaired microvascular function. Crucially, these neurovascular impairments were reversed by daily administration of an endothelin receptor antagonist during IH exposure, with the exception of pial vein constriction. In conclusion, reduced cerebral perfusion after chronic IH is associated with persistent narrowing of parenchymal venules and pial veins. These findings provide new insights into the cerebral microvascular complications of chronic IH and suggest the potential utility of neurovascular protective agents.

papers.title: Association of Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet with sleep quality and quantity, inflammation and oxidative stress in Iranian adults: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Although some studies have examined the relation of Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet with sleep disorders, their results were inconclusive and none of them considered inflammation and oxidative stress biomarkers as potential contributors. We evaluated the relation between MIND diet and sleep parameters in Iranian adults, taking biomarkers into account. A sample of 535 adults (46 % were female), with a mean age of 42·6 years, was selected via a multistage-cluster random sampling for this cross-sectional investigation. Dietary data were collected via a validated FFQ. Sleep quality and sleep duration were assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire. Concentration of biomarkers was assessed using participants' blood samples, taken after a period of night-fasting. In fully-adjusted model, participants in the highest (v. lowest) tertile of MIND diet had 54 % lower odds of short sleeping (ORT3v.T1 = 0·46, 95 % CI: 0·22-0·93), and subjects in the highest tertile of MIND score had 56 % lower odds of poor sleep quality (ORT3v.T1 = 0·44, 95 % CI: 0·21-0·95). These associations were stronger in participants with overweight and obesity. Higher adherence to MIND was associated with a lower probability of sleep disturbance (ORT3v.T1 = 0·27, 95 % CI: 0·08-0·89). There was no statistically significant association between the MIND diet and either oxidative stress or inflammatory biomarkers (P > 0·05). These findings highlighted inverse associations between higher MIND adherence and sleep disorders among Iranian adults. No significant associations between MIND adherence and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress were found.

papers.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Syndromic autism refers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) occurring as part of an identifiable genetic syndrome. Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome (HVDAS/ADNP syndrome) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the ADNP gene. We report a 10-year-old boy with ASD and intellectual disability who exhibited delayed motor and language development, characteristic facial dysmorphism, early tooth eruption, endocrine abnormalities, electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities, and urogenital findings. Following unremarkable karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic de novo frameshift variant, c.1239_1240del, p.(Gln414Valfs*25) in ADNP. This case emphasizes the importance of considering a syndromic etiology in children with ASD accompanied by developmental delay, dysmorphic features, neurological findings, or multisystem involvement, and supports comprehensive genetic evaluation when first-tier testing is unrevealing.

papers.title: Altered Timing of Self-Voice Processing in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) affects voice and speech production, often resulting in reduced vocal intensity and monotonous speech. Recent studies suggest that these changes can be partially explained by altered sensory feedback processing in speech production: individuals with PD (IwPD) may fail to monitor and adapt sensory feedback when producing speech. We investigated PD voice production using a voice playback paradigm and focused on the sensory attenuation typically observed in event-related responses (ERPs) to the self-generated voice. When sensory feedback is intact, the P50, N100, and P200 responses to a self-generated voice are attenuated compared to an externally generated voice. Twenty-three IwPD and 23 matched healthy controls (HCs) completed the voice playback study with three conditions: self-generated voice (auditory-motor [AMC]), externally generated voice (auditory-only [AOC]), and motor-only. Linear mixed models assessed group differences in ERP morphology. Groups differed in the N100 latency response: IwPD showed a greater shift in latency between AMC and AOC than healthy controls. Regarding the P200, a significant group-by-condition interaction indicated that IwPD, unlike healthy controls, produced larger amplitudes for the self-generated than the passively listened to voice. Taken together, these findings suggest that the processing of one's own voice in IwPD is altered in terms of temporal precision rather than in the N100 suppression effect per se. This effect was accompanied by an enhanced P200 attentional response. These response patterns in IwPD are indicative of likely progressing difficulties in regulating one's own voice, characteristic of Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Exploring patient experiences of same-day discharge after hip and knee arthroplasty: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: This study explored and compared patient experiences of same-day discharge (SDD) following total hip (THA) and knee arthroplasty (TKA) in South Africa's private healthcare sector, aiming to understand perceptions, recovery processes, and implications for rehabilitation. A qualitative design using semi-structured interviews was undertaken with participants following SDD THA and TKA. Interviews were conducted 6 weeks postoperatively. Data from each procedure group were analyzed independently using inductive thematic analysis before comparative analysis. Trustworthiness was enhanced through triangulation, peer debriefing, and member checks. Twenty-four participants (THA: n = 14; TKA: n = 10) were interviewed. Participants reported high satisfaction with SDD, with structured care, interdisciplinary (IDT) support, and preoperative education facilitating recovery. However, procedure-specific differences were identified. THA participants emphasized emotional reassurance, relational support, and intrinsic motivation, whereas TKA participants described greater physical challenges, particularly pain, mobility limitations, and sleep disturbance. Effective pain management, caregiver support, and coordinated interdisciplinary care were important across both groups. SDD was positively experienced within this South African private healthcare setting, but recovery experiences differed meaningfully between THA and TKA. These findings support procedure-specific rehabilitation pathways, incorporating common elements of preparation and interdisciplinary care while addressing the differing physical, functional, and emotional priorities associated with THA and TKA recovery.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Exploratory Pharmacodynamics of Melanin-Concentrating Hormone Receptor-1 Antagonist RGH-706 in Healthy and Overweight or Obese Men.
papers.abstract: This Phase 1 program evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and exploratory pharmacodynamics of the novel melanin-concentrating hormone receptor-1 antagonist RGH-706. Study A was a first-in-man, randomized trial comprising a double-blind, placebo-controlled single-ascending-dose part (0.1-162.5 mg) and a two-way crossover food-effect assessment at 62.5 mg in healthy men. Study B was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single- and multiple-ascending-dose study in overweight or obese (otherwise healthy) men receiving a single dose followed by 14 days of once-daily dosing (2.5-22.5 mg/day). Safety assessments included clinical evaluations, ECGs and mood and sleep scales. RGH-706 concentrations in plasma and urine samples were measured by validated methods. Pharmacokinetics was characterized using non-compartmental analysis. Study B evaluated exploratory pharmacodynamic measures including appetite-related outcomes, food preference, test-meal food and macronutrient intake, body composition and metabolic biomarkers. In Study A (n = 68), systemic exposure increased approximately dose proportionally up to 62.5 mg and more than proportionally above, with tmax between 2.5 and 3.5 h and a bi-exponential disposition with a 29-35 h terminal half-life. Food ingestion had a negligible effect on exposure and renal clearance was also negligible. In Study B (n = 36), RGH-706 showed moderate accumulation with steady state reached within 8 days. Exploratory pharmacodynamic measures showed a trend towards lower total energy intake, preference for fatty foods and weight gain, primarily with the lower doses of 2.5 and 7.5 mg/day. RGH-706 was well tolerated across all doses and conditions in both studies. RGH-706 was safe, well tolerated and exhibited well-characterized pharmacokinetics. The pharmacodynamic data support further exploration of RGH-706 in weight management.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.abstract: Irritability is characterized by a propensity to experience frustration and has been associated with reduced self-reported willingness to expend effort for rewards. Frustration may be relevant to effortful reward pursuit, but its effects on effort expenditure have rarely been experimentally tested in humans. To address this gap, this study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task to elicit frustrative nonreward (FNR), a negative emotional state triggered by unexpected reward loss, and examined its effects on physical effort expenditure and feedback-related electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. We also tested whether these effects vary as a function of state and trait measures of motivation and affect. Linear mixed-effects models tested the effects of FNR induction on self-reported, behavioral, and EEG measures in young adults (N = 83) completing the Frustrative Effort-Doors task. Models tested manipulation effects, trial-level post-feedback adjustment, and moderation by state and trait measures. Midfrontal theta power (MFθ) extracted using multivariate spatial filtering was examined as a function of feedback (win vs. FNR), effort (low vs. high), and subsequent behavioral adjustments. The frustration condition was associated with decreased self-reported state motivation and increased frustration, arousal, and response speed. Midfrontal theta power was larger following FNR feedback and increased with state frustration during high-effort trials. Higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following FNR feedback. MFθ did not predict trial-to-trial behavioral adjustments. These findings indicate that FNR recruits MFθ, a neural marker of cognitive control, while state frustration modulates physical effort execution following unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: Inclusive electroencephalography practices for Black and Muslim participation in a White non-Muslim-majority country: A co-produced tutorial.
papers.abstract: Most electroencephalography (EEG) research is conducted in White-majority Western countries by White researchers. EEG practices therefore often explicitly and implicitly exclude minoritised groups, leading to low diversity in EEG data samples that deepens biases in interpretation and clinical utility. Because EEG electrodes must contact the scalp, Black people and Muslim women who wear a hijab (or, Hijabis) are two systematically excluded groups. As a group of EEG researchers, Black people, and Hijabis, here we describe co-produced practical approaches to overcoming EEG participation barriers, from recruitment to data collection, and provide co-produced text, photographs, and videos designed to break down these barriers. These approaches provide further tools for the EEG community to tackle systemic exclusion and foster better, more representative neuroscience.

papers.title: Risk factors associated with hypertension in patients attending a pediatric sleep clinic: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension due to an interplay of factors. Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH). However, ABPM is not routinely performed. We aim to detect hypertension using ABPM and to identify risk factors associated with hypertension. This was a prospective cohort study of pediatric patients (5-18 years of age) who had been referred to the sleep clinic. Polysomnography (PSG) or overnight pulse oximetry (OPO) were performed as per standard of care. ABPM was performed for all recruited patients. The primary outcome was hypertension, i.e., ambulatory hypertension or MH. Sixty-eight patients were recruited. Median age was 12.6 (interquartile range [IQR] 10.0-14.7) years. Fourteen (21%) did not return for the ABPM and ten (15%) had insufficient readings. Of the remaining 44 patients with complete ABPM data, hypertension was diagnosed in 18/44 (41%) with 10 (23%) having ambulatory hypertension and 8 (18%) having MH. Among the 18 patients with hypertension, one defaulted sleep study; 3/17 (18%) had primary snoring; 6/17 (35%), 4/17 (24%), and 4/17 (24%) had mild, moderate, and severe OSA, respectively. The prevalence of hypertension was 6/20 (30%), 4/10 (40%), 4/8 (50%), and 3/5 (60%) among patients with mild, moderate, and severe OSA and primary snoring, respectively. Age (relative risk [RR] 1.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.52, p = 0.008) and primary snoring (RR 3.52, 95% CI 1.38-8.97, p = 0.004) were independently associated with hypertension. Increasing age and primary snoring may be independently associated with hypertension among pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic. Larger studies will be required to validate these risk factors. • Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension which is often due to an interplay of multiple factors. • Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH). • In this prospective single-center study, ABPM was performed for all patients, classifying hypertension based on the 2022 update on ABPM in children from the American Heart Association. • Increasing age and primary snoring were independently associated with hypertension in pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic.

papers.title: Near-Zero Creep Ionic Elastomer for Non-drifting Ear Electroencephalogram Signal Acquisition.
papers.abstract: Monitoring and identification of ear electroencephalogram (Ear-EEG) signals offer a promising non-invasive approach for tracking mental states. Compared to rigid metal electrodes, polymer electrodes possess flexibility, good biocompatibility, superior skin adhesion, and wearing comfort, however, their accuracy is often compromised by signal drift due to polymer creep under sustained strain. To address this, we introduce a molecular strategy that suppresses creep by compensating entropy loss through a designed intramolecular dihedral structure. The copolymer integrates two distinct crosslinks: flexible segments stabilized by electrostatic self-coordination, and a minority of rigid segments formed by covalent main-chain bridges. In-situ scattering and theoretical simulations confirm that the covalently bridged TAO segments adopt a rigid dihedral configuration, effectively restraining chain slippage and eradicating viscoelasticity. Concurrently, dynamic disulfide exchange further enhances network stability under deformation. This design yields the near-zero creep polyelectrolyte ionic elastomer, denoted as Poly(TA-co-TAT)-TAO, which demonstrates remarkable stretchability (>200%) and elasticity (hysteresis <7.5%, recovery >99% at 160% strain). Leveraging its persistent creep resistance (<0.4% over 12 hours), the resulting wearable EEG device enables reliable, long-term mental status monitoring in real-world settings.

papers.title: Profound Tacrolimus-Induced Catatonic Encephalopathy in a Kidney Transplant Recipient With Mitochondrial Myopathy: A Cautionary Case of Reversible Neurotoxicity.
papers.abstract: Maternally inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD) is a multisystem mitochondrial disorder most commonly caused by the m.3243A>G pathogenic variant in the MT-TL1 gene. Kidney transplantation in affected individuals presents unique perioperative and immunosuppressive management challenges due to underlying metabolic, neurologic, cardiac, and neuromuscular vulnerability. We report a 64-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease secondary to insulin-dependent diabetes and MIDD (m.3243A>G) who underwent unrelated living donor kidney transplantation. The immediate postoperative period was complicated by diabetic ketoacidosis with lactic acidosis, transient slow graft function, and profound encephalopathy with catatonic features. Neuroimaging showed no acute abnormalities, and electroencephalography demonstrated severe diffuse encephalopathy without epileptiform activity. Tacrolimus levels were supratherapeutic in the early postoperative period. Given concern for calcineurin inhibitor neurotoxicity superimposed on mitochondrial dysfunction, tacrolimus was discontinued, and immunosuppression was switched to cyclosporine. Neurologic status gradually improved, and kidney allograft function fully normalized. This case highlights the substantial perioperative metabolic and neurologic risks associated with kidney transplantation in patients with MIDD. Patients with compensated cardiac dysfunction and manageable neuromuscular impairment should not be excluded from transplantation solely on the basis of mitochondrial cytopathy.

papers.title: Tracking newly synthesised proteins in plants.
papers.abstract: Protein synthesis rate is distinct from steady-state protein abundance and must be measured independently to understand how cells regulate protein levels and respond to environments. Technologies used to predict or directly quantify protein synthesis include ribosome profiling, radioactive and stable isotope labelling, and bioorthogonal noncanonical amino acid tagging (BONCAT). Here, we emphasise BONCAT's potential in plants, which, when combined with click-chemistry, enables the detection, enrichment, and characterisation of newly synthesised proteins themselves. We summarise lessons from BONCAT applications in cell-free systems, microbes, mammalian cells, and animals and evaluate its potential in plants. Establishing robust BONCAT approaches in plants can advance studies in proteome regulation, stress responses, development, circadian biology, and plant-microbe interactions.

papers.title: High-Frequency Low-Tidal Volume Ventilation and Procedural Efficiency in Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation. Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study. Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital. There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024. Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia. Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference. In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.
papers.journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

papers.title: A brain circuit linking sleep loss to pain.
papers.abstract: Sleep loss heightens pain sensitivity, but the brain circuits involved remain unclear. In a recent study, Huang, Wang, Jiao, and colleagues identified a pathway connecting the retrosplenial cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and zona incerta that contributes to heightened sensitivity to mechanical stimulation and heat after sleep deprivation in male mice.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Actigraphy-based sleep outcomes in substance use disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis" [Sleep Med Rev 88, 102297].
Sleep-related Brain Activity in an Arousal-reducing Agent-induced Mouse Model Evaluated with fMRI.
papers.abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has been established as a technique for capturing functional changes based on brain activity and is widely used to evaluate various diseases and physiological conditions. However, studies that systematically evaluate functional brain networks during arousal-reducing agent-induced sleep in mice by using resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) are limited. This study aimed to compare and analyze whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) and reorganization patterns of large-scale brain functional networks in the mouse brain during arousal-reducing agent-induced sleep, focusing on arousal-reducing agents acting on different arousal regulatory systems. Sixteen healthy male C57BL/6JmsSlc mice (aged 16.4 ± 8.7 week) were used in this study. The mice were assigned to 4 groups: control, zolpidem (20 mg/kg), lemborexant (40 mg/kg), and dexmedetomidine (75 μg/kg). rsfMRI was performed using a 9.4T MRI system equipped with an 86 mm volume transmit coil and an 8-channel receive-only coil (Bruker BioSpin, Ettlingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany). After head post-surgery and habituation, blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) images were acquired using a gradient-echo echo-planar imaging (GRE-EPI) sequence (TR/TE = 1500/14 ms). Each mouse underwent six 10 min imaging sessions. fMRI data were preprocessed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12; Wellcome Centre for Human Neuroimaging, London, UK) and analyzed using the CONN FC toolbox (McGovern Institute for Brain Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA). ROI × ROI FC matrices were calculated for each fMRI session. Group differences were assessed using linear mixed-effects models that accounted for repeated measurements within animals, individual variability, and age differences among groups. Compared to the control group, the zolpidem group showed the smallest overall differences, whereas the dexmedetomidine group showed the largest differences. Furthermore, although relatively similar trends were observed between the groups in the distribution of mean correlation coefficients within each network, different trends were observed between the networks. In addition to network reorganization associated with the sleep-inducing state, which is commonly observed regardless of the arousal-reducing agent type, distinct network changes exhibiting arousal-reducing agent-specific connectivity patterns were observed.

papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Integration of Video and EEG Reveals Distinct Seizure Phenotypes in Mouse Models of Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Video-electrocorticogram (VEEG) recordings are the gold-standard diagnostic tool for detecting and characterizing seizures in rodent models of seizure and epilepsy. Manual/visual scoring remains the prevailing strategy despite significant limitations. Alternatively, automated and semi-automated analyses have been applied to either EEG or video features alone but integrating these disparate data forms presents a challenge that has not been sufficiently addressed. Here, we introduce an integrated machine learning pipeline that jointly leverages EEG and behavioral video data to enable scalable and objective event classification. Integrated video-EEG analysis was initially validated using a well-established pharmacologically induced seizure paradigm in male mice, where overt generalized motor seizures provide a clear benchmark. We then tested the pipeline on a genetic mouse model of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) that displays a complex spike-wave discharge (SWD) seizure phenotype that poses significant challenges for traditional scoring methods. Machine learning-powered integrated analysis of video-EEG recordings outperformed unimodal EEG- or video-based approaches and performed favorably to experienced rodent EEG electrophysiologists while also uncovering distinct phenotypic relationships, including classes of atypical behavioral and typical non-behavioral SWD events. This framework provides a flexible tool for high-throughput, precise analysis of VEEG data, with potential to accelerate discovery in epilepsy and seizure research. Furthermore, this approach represents a generalizable strategy for the integration of diverse neurobehavioral time series data types.Significance Statement Seizure detection in animal models of epilepsy has relied heavily on manual analysis of video-EEG recordings, a process that is slow and subjective. We present a machine learning pipeline that integrates EEG and video data from mice to classify seizures with high accuracy. This work was validated across two models, first a pharmacologically induced generalized seizure model, and second, a spontaneous spike-wave discharge (SWD) model in genetic epilepsy. Our approach detected events missed by human reviewers and revealed previously uncharacterized SWD subtypes distinguished by their behavior. By combining open-source tools in a flexible framework, this work lowers the barrier to high-throughput, unbiased seizure phenotyping, and also offers a broadly applicable strategy for linking neural activity to behavior in neuroscience research.

papers.title: Microglial Presenilin-1 modulates neuronal function and memory-associated behaviors.
papers.abstract: Microglial cells, the macrophages of the brain parenchyma, are increasingly recognized to play a key role in synaptic plasticity and function. Presenilin 1 (PS1) is an essential protein involved in learning and memory; the loss of neuronal Presenilin function causes cognitive deficits and impaired synapse plasticity in mice. Here we show memory enhancement in male mice lacking PS1 in microglia (PS1ΔMG). Leveraging high-throughput RNA sequencing with single-cell deconvolution-analysis, we estimate that PS1ΔMG increases Cd52-lo microglial population, a proliferative group enriched in AP-1 responsive genes; and increases chemokines Ccl7 and Ccl8 In silico prediction of binding partners showed that microglial CCL7 may act via inhibition of neuronal CCR5, a receptor known to negatively regulate learning and memory. By profiling active neuronal populations via PhosphoTRAP the data showed a non-autonomous cell effect of microglial PS1 by modulating genes involved in neuronal excitability and synaptic plasticity. Ex vivo electrophysiology and in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving mice confirm these effects with functional changes in CA1 hippocampus as seen by increased NMDA/AMPA ratios and increased amplitude of neuronal Ca2+ transients in freely behaving animals, respectively. Remarkably, PS1ΔMG mice exhibited increased memory retention in contextual fear conditioning and novel object recognition. Together, these data suggest a novel mechanism where microglial PS1 negatively regulates neuronal activity through modulation of NMDAR and memory-associated behaviors.Significance Statement Microglia are increasingly recognized as active regulators of neuronal function, yet the molecular mechanisms that constrain their influence on synaptic activity remain incompletely defined. This study identifies microglial Presenilin-1 (PS1) as a key regulator of neuron-microglia signaling that shapes synaptic transmission and learning. We show that loss of microglial PS1 shifts microglia toward a transcriptional and signaling state that enhances NMDA receptor-dependent synaptic activity and improves memory, demonstrating that microglial molecular programs can directly modulate neuronal excitability. These findings establish microglial PS1 as a physiological brake on circuit plasticity and reveal that altering microglial signaling alone is sufficient to influence cognition. Targeting microglial regulatory pathways may therefore provide new strategies to enhance synaptic resilience and cognitive function in brain disorders.

papers.title: iGABASnFR Imaging Reveals that GABA Clearance is rapidly overwhelmed in the Cerebral Cortex.
papers.abstract: Both phasic and tonic GABAergic activity in the cortex, is shaped by the clearance of GABA from the extracellular space by GABA transporters (GATs). However, estimates of the time-course of GAT activity from GAT currents, GABAA, and GABAB electrophysiological recordings range from tens of milliseconds to multiple seconds. These estimates may reflect receptor properties rather than extracellular GABA dynamics. Understanding how long GABA is free in the extracellular space is key to understanding how inhibition controls activity, but has been technically challenging. Here, we utilize the fluorescent GABA sensor, iGABASnFr, to enable us to optically assay extracellular GABA dynamics following bursts of synaptic activity. In the mouse cerebral cortex of either sex, we show that GABA rapidly disperses from release sites via diffusion, with very little role for active transport by GATs. Following diffusion from the sites of release, GABA then accumulates in the extracellular space, where GATs require hundreds of milliseconds to remove it. For areas of high density GABA release or during bursts of activity, this clearance is further slowed. Continued GABA release and summation in the extracellular space for bursts of activity contrasts with recorded Inhibitory post-synaptic current (IPSC) signals, which rapidly depress with additional stimuli, suggesting a disconnect between IPSCs and extracellular GABA. Lastly, the resulting extracellular accumulation of GABA can act hetero-synaptically by activating and/or desensitizing GABAA receptors. Together, this raises new questions about how GABAergic inhibition works to shape network function and suggests a spatiotemporal continuum of extracellular GABA.Significance Statement We use combined iGABASnFr neurotransmitter imaging, electrophysiology, and modeling to show that with trains of synaptic activity, GABA clearance is slowed and GABA rapidly accumulates in the extracellular space. Additionally, we demonstrate that GABA largely diffuses from release sites rather than being captured by GABA transporters and that these transporters have only a small role in shaping extracellular GABA dynamics in the mouse cortex. Lastly, we show that extracellular GABA accumulation can heterosynaptically desensitize GABAA receptors, modulating local phasic inhibition.
